hero.h1: A private mind for your meetings.
hero.sub: Sonabrief records, transcribes, and summarizes your professional conversations — without sending a single byte of audio to the cloud. Ever.
hero.micro: Free plan available · No credit card · Open source

lines: Every meeting tool sends your audio to servers you've never seen.

items.title: Your audio stays on your computer.
items.body: Processed in memory, transcribed, discarded. Never saved. Never uploaded.

items.title: Your notes are encrypted before sync.
items.body: We can't read them. Neither can our cloud LLM. Twelve words protect your archive.

items.title: Open source.

Whisper Large-v3-turbo — the same model researchers use — is available on every plan, including Free, and runs entirely on your machine. memory.lead: Most meeting tools delete your history after 14 days on free plans. We think your professional memory should belong to you — not their retention policy.
memory.body: Encrypted with your passphrase. Synced across your devices. Searchable. Yours — really yours.
memory.tradeoff: If you forget your passphrase, we can't recover it. Trade-offs are real. We don't hide them.

professionals.lead: We built this for people whose conversations carry real weight.
professionals.close: If your meetings contain things the cloud shouldn't see, you understand exactly why we built this.
professionals.aside: (If they don't — Sonabrief works for you too.)

enterprise.heading: Enterprise
enterprise.body: Custom pricing for teams. Self-hosted option available, with a commercial license (an alternative to AGPL v3) for modified self-hosted deployments. SSO, admin dashboard, dedicated support.

items.a: If Sonabrief isn't right for you, email hello@sonabrief.com within 14 days of your payment and we'll refund it — annual plans included. No forms, no friction.

Anything older than your new plan's retention limit stays available for 30 more days, marked as expiring — time to export it or change your mind. After that it's removed. Your audio was never stored, so there's nothing else to clean up.

Prices are shown without VAT. At checkout our payment provider, Polar, acts as merchant of record and applies the correct VAT for your country; your invoice includes it. Have a VAT number? Enter it at checkout.

Monthly plans renew each month on your signup date. Annual plans renew once a year and include two months free. Cancel anytime from your account — the next charge stops and you keep access until the period ends.

items.q: Can I share one account with my team?
items.a: Accounts are personal. Pro Unlimited adds multi-device so you can use your own account across all your machines. For several people, Enterprise offers a proper multi-seat setup — get in touch.
No. The Free plan is real, with unlimited local transcription — that already covers a lot. We'd rather keep pricing simple than run special cases.

items.q: Do you ever upload my audio anywhere?
items.a: No. Audio is processed in memory on your device, transcribed, then discarded. It never reaches our servers, not even as a temporary file. You can verify this in our code — the specific function is linked on our /security page.

items.q: What are the three transcription modes?
items.a: Standard transcribes locally and summarizes in the EU cloud. Local Only keeps everything on your machine. Cloud Fast (Pro and Pro Unlimited) transcribes through Mistral's EU servers in Paris — fast on any hardware, with audio encrypted in transit and never saved. You choose per meeting.

items.q: What if I forget my passphrase?
items.a: We can't recover it — that's the point of zero-knowledge encryption. During onboarding you receive 12 recovery words (BIP39 standard). Write them down and store them safely. If you lose both the passphrase and the recovery words, your encrypted archive becomes unreadable. Trade-offs are real.

items.q: Is your cloud LLM really EU-hosted?
items.a: Yes. We use Mistral, an EU company, on EU-hosted infrastructure, with Zero Data Retention active and a signed Data Processing Agreement. Details and the DPA reference on /security.
Because privacy promises that can't be verified are marketing. Everything that handles your data is on GitHub under AGPL v3. Read it, audit it, fork it.

The Free plan exists and is real — not crippled. Pro is for people who need longer history, better LLM quality, and the full feature set. We need revenue to stay independent and maintain the infrastructure. Simple.
Sonabrief is a progressive web app — install it from your browser on any device. Recording from mobile is coming in a future update. Sync and archive reading work today on mobile.
UI available in English, Italian, French, Spanish, German. Transcription: 99 languages via Whisper. Summary templates: EN, IT, FR, ES, DE at launch.
Now. Create your free account above.

promise.title: The promise
lines: Your meeting audio is never saved as a file.
Everything derived from it — transcripts, summaries, notes — lives where you decide: encrypted on our servers with zero-knowledge, on your machine only, or both.

audio.title: What happens to your audio
flow: Transcribed by Whisper in short batches
audio.body: No audio file — no .wav, .mp3, or .webm — is ever written to disk. Ever. During recording, audio is held in memory; to survive a browser crash in a long meeting, short batches live for a couple of minutes in your browser's encrypted local database and erase themselves the moment they're transcribed. By the end of the meeting, no audio remains anywhere.
audio.codeNote: This isn't a marketing claim. The exact function that discards your audio is in our open source code.

zeroKnowledge.title: Zero-knowledge sync
zeroKnowledge.intro: When you sync, your notes and summaries are encrypted before they leave your device.

points.plain: Your 12 recovery words become your encryption key through Argon2id, a deliberately slow key-derivation function. This is exactly why, if you forget your passphrase, no one — including us — can recover it.
Your data is sealed with XChaCha20-Poly1305, the same authenticated-encryption primitive used by WhatsApp and Signal.
All of this happens on your device, before anything reaches our servers.

zeroKnowledge.closer: What we store is encrypted data we cannot read. Not because we choose not to — because we mathematically can't.

subprocessors.note: Where a subprocessor is US-based, it never processes readable meeting content — only the limited data listed. Your meetings stay on your device or are encrypted so that neither we nor they can read them.

verify.title: Verify it yourself
verify.intro: Don't take our word for it.
steps: Start a recording in Standard or Local Only mode.
Open your browser's DevTools — Network tab.

Record for 30 seconds and watch the outbound requests. In Local Only, nothing leaves your device at all; in Standard, only text — the transcription result — never audio. (Cloud Fast is different by design: there, encrypted audio is sent to our EU servers to be transcribed, encrypted in transit and never saved. That's the one mode where seeing audio leave is expected.)

early.title: We are early
early.body: We're a small, independent product. We don't publish aggregate transparency metrics yet — our user base is still too small for the numbers to mean anything. We will, when they do. Until then, our code is the proof.

sections.title: Why we built this
sections.body: Years working across professional services taught us how much sensitive information flows through meeting rooms — and how little control people have over where it ends up. Existing tools made a trade we couldn't accept: convenience in exchange for control over your own conversations. We wanted both. So we built Sonabrief.

sections.title: Why open source
sections.body: Open source is the proof that what we say matches what we do. Read it, audit it, fork it. AGPL v3.

sections.title: Why bootstrap
sections.body: No VC, no growth-at-all-costs. We pay our bills with subscriptions. That's the model.

sections.title: Why we don't show our face
sections.body: The brand speaks for itself. When Sonabrief needs a public face, it'll have one. Until then: hello@sonabrief.com.

sections.title: What we won't build
items: Meeting tools that compromise privacy "just for free users"
Enterprise bloat that makes the product worse for individuals
Analytics that spy on you to sell ads
Anything that would require us to be less honest tomorrow than we are today

openSourcePage.intro: Everything that handles your data is open source. Not a gesture — the way we prove our privacy promises.

sections.title: What's open
sections.body: All the code that touches your data — recording, transcription, encryption, sync — is public on GitHub.

sections.title: AGPL v3, in practice
sections.body: You're free to read, run, and fork Sonabrief. Distribute a modified version and AGPL v3 asks you to share your changes under the same license. Commercial distribution without those obligations needs a separate license.

sections.title: The Harmony CLA
sections.body: Contributors sign a Contributor License Agreement (Harmony CLA). It lets us keep offering a commercial license to Enterprise customers alongside the open source one, while your contribution stays open.

sections.title: Dual licensing
sections.body: Enterprise customers can choose a commercial license — an alternative to AGPL v3 — for modified self-hosted deployments.

sections.title: How to contribute
sections.body: Read CONTRIBUTING.md, open an issue, or send a pull request. Everything happens in the open.
